claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as scary, particularly during nighttime gameplay.

citations.review_text:
Last time I ever was scared shirtless playing a game was around the age of 12, playing F.E.A.R 2.

The closest another game has ever got to that was RE7. 

Resident Evil (while a great game), couldn't manage to instill that pure fear - the jumpscares made me flinch - but it never made me properly scared.

Well, 0 expectations, got this game off the Summer sale and gave it a try last night.

Everything was pretty straightforward, come the mission about setting up traps/turning on some lights. 

♥♥♥♥. And I say ♥♥♥♥.

You know that feeling when you were a kid and afraid of the dark?

It's that, but WORSE. 

This game is deceptively welcoming during the day, but when my first night came.. jesuuus. 

It's the type of experience where you get goosebumps, being afraid to look behind.

10/10, and I'm only 1 hour in.

sh1tting my pants. 10/10 recommend

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Early players enjoy cooperative multiplayer and the parkour combat loop while navigating a tense day and night cycle, despite a weak campaign and degrading weapons.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the day and night cycle creates a stark contrast in gameplay tension, turning a safe daytime playground into a dangerous nighttime environment.

citations.review_text: one of the best zombie survival experiences in gaming, defined by its industry-leading parkour and terrifying day-night cycles.

Dying Light is a game that released during one of the worst possible times for a zombie game. The market was overflowing with undead apocalypse titles, and because of that, I think this game got unfairly buried in the massive pile of zombie fatigue.
Which is a shame, because the concept behind this game is brilliant.
The marriage of parkour, zombies, and a terrifying night cycle is something that should not have worked as well as it did. Running across rooftops during the day feels empowering. You are fast, agile, and in control. Then the sun goes down and suddenly everything changes. The safety disappears. The infected become faster, stronger, and far more terrifying. The entire city transforms from your playground into a place you are desperately trying to survive.
That contrast is what makes Dying Light special.
Unfortunately, the story did absolutely nothing for me. The moment I heard Kyle Crane's completely sleepwalked voice delivery, I knew I was not here for the narrative. Every emotional moment felt like it was fighting against a protagonist who sounded like he was reading a grocery list.
But honestly?
I did not care.
I cared about unlocking the grappling hook.
I cared about upgrading my movement.
I cared about drop kicking zombies off rooftops and seeing how much chaos I could create.
That is where Dying Light shines. The gameplay loop is addictive because moving through the world is just as satisfying as fighting through it. The city becomes your playground, and every rooftop, alleyway, and abandoned building becomes an opportunity for another ridiculous moment.
Few games make you feel the urge to simply move around because the movement itself is fun.
Dying Light does.
It is a shame this game arrived during peak zombie oversaturation because underneath all the familiar apocalypse themes is one of the most unique zombie experiences ever created.
A parkour simulator.
A zombie survival simulator.
A "one more dropkick before I turn the game off" simulator.

👍 Recommended

Dying Light is easily one of the best zombie survival games ever made. The parkour system feels smooth and satisfying, making movement around the city incredibly fun. Combat is brutal, progression is rewarding, and every weapon feels impactful.

What truly sets the game apart is its day and night cycle. During the day, you can explore and scavenge with confidence, but once the sun goes down, the game becomes a completely different experience. The tension, atmosphere, and sense of danger at night are unmatched.

The story is decent, but the gameplay is what keeps you hooked for dozens of hours. Whether playing solo or with friends, Dying Light delivers an unforgettable zombie survival experience.

Even after all these years, it remains one of the strongest entries in the zombie genre.

9/10 – Worth every minute.

citations.review_text:
Even though I played it a bit late compared to its release year, I can clearly say this: It was already a perfect game for its time, and it still holds up incredibly well today. Before buying it, I was like, "I’ll probably play for 10 hours max and leave it." Well, I ended up spending nearly 20 hours all by myself smashing zombies in Harran and the Texas-like countryside. The game just sucks you in.

I rushed through it a bit by focusing strictly on the main stories; I finished the main game in 10 hours, and the The Following DLC took me another 10 hours. But don't let this fool you. There are so many side quests, random events, and safe zones to clear. On top of that, you can jump into online co-op to raise hell with friends, or play the "Be the Zombie" mode to become the monster yourself and invade other players' games. If you actually take your time and do everything, this game can easily offer up to 100 hours of gameplay. The content is massive.

Main Game, Story & Atmosphere:
The story is pure chaos. I got so incredibly pissed off at that piece of sh*t organization called the GRE and that scumbag warlord Rais. They constantly used us like pawns for their own selfish interests and didn't care about humanity at all. The thing that hurt the most in the story was definitely Jade <3... When she sacrificed herself and handed us that last dose of Antizin with her own hands, it genuinely broke my heart.

But leaping from roof to roof doing parkour in Harran was still a blast. Not to mention the mini heart attacks I suffered from Volatiles chasing me at night. During the day, you're confidently running at zombies, but once night falls, you turn into a terrified runner frantically searching the map for a safe house. The mechanics, combat impact, and zombie variety are excellent.

The Following DLC & Endings:
The DLC completely evolves the game. Leaving parkour behind and jumping into the buggy turned the game into a pure zombie-crushing simulator. Especially that whole m…

I love the slightly different take on a zombie game. The heavy parkour element makes it stand out a lot. Sadly the campaign is pretty short, only took me 15 hours to beat but if you grab it on sale then can't complain!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe combat involving weapons that degrade and break down over time during use.

citations.review_text: It was probably considered good in it's day, but this aged horribly. Clunky combat, poorly conceived set pieces and NPCs that have that 2010s feel. A crafting system that feels meaningless given how much stuff you can carry around and how abundant the raw materials are, makes it feel more like a time sink that a challenging way to aquire weapons and gear. One for the dustbin of history. The parkour is fine I guess.

Highly Recommended ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

I've played almost every Resident Evil game there is, and nothing else has come close — until Dying Light.

This game delivers an extraordinarily realistic experience as an ordinary survivor: the fear of zombies, fighting with weapons that break down on you, the fear of heights while scaling buildings, the fear of zombie chasing in the night. It's an open world where zombies chase you from every direction, and the AI is genuinely smart — they flank you, they swarm you, they hunt. You must run and Parkour around.

You loot resources to craft items. You have low stamina to run & fight. You quietly walk around evade zombie. You find your own way to complete your mission. You are a real person just trying to survive and fight.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the campaign features repetitive side quests that consist mainly of fetch tasks.

citations.review_text: I played it for the first time. It wasn't really my kind of game. It started off interestingly, but the story didn't impress me later on. The gameplay was fun overall, but I’m not a fan of parkour, and the character's movement could be annoying at times. There were also way too many repetitive side quests (run here, fetch that) with lackluster rewards. On top of that, the map was bloated with activities; for a player who likes to explore thoroughly and complete everything, it felt tedious and exhausting. Ultimately, I didn't enjoy the game much—it felt like a slog. I wouldn't replay it, and I probably won't touch the sequel.

Weapon upgrades really only increment the damage number sizing while make absolutely no difference to gameplay at all, making the combat very-samey through the whole game and the story is fetch after fetch while ignoring most enemies.

Firstly, I’d like to say that I’m not a huge fan of horror games. Obviously, when zombies are trying to bite you, the adrenaline really kicks in. I also played on the lowest difficulty because I wanted to focus on enjoying the story and exploration. Did the game deliver? Definitely.

The game was released back in 2015, so about 11 years ago. I previously played the Dead Island series, which I enjoyed, but this gem takes things to a whole new level. The city is highly detailed, and the parkour system feels spot-on. As you progress, you gain experience and unlock skills across different trees (Survivor, Agility, Power, and Driver). Crafting is also a major part of the game and can significantly make things easier. You’ll find plenty of locked chests containing weapons or components, which you can use to craft upgrades like electricity or fire mods. You can also use crossbows, pistols, or rifles, although I personally preferred firearms only against armed human enemies to resolve encounters more efficiently.

The story is rich, and as expected in an apocalypse setting, many characters won’t survive. Some missions can feel a bit repetitive, but the game offers a large number of side quests to keep things interesting. What surprised me the most was the introduction of the second major location during the main story. Just as I started to feel a bit bored of the Slums (the first area), progressing the story unlocked a new region—Old Town—which completely refreshed the experience. It felt like a second wind for my playthrough: a new environment, new side quests, new characters, and new weapons. Techland handled this transition wonderfully.

Of course, being a zombie game, you won’t spend all your time in sunny areas. Missions take you through sewers, dark houses, and abandoned hospitals without electricity, which adds to the atmosphere.

Where the game truly excels is parkour. The feeling of successfully chaining jumps, slides, and grapples is incredibly satisfying. It’s no…

citations.review_text:
ꨄ My rating: 8/10 ꨄ

Pros:
- The artstyle of this game is very good, features a moody apocalyptic environment that looks abandoned and completely overrun by zombies. At night this game suddendly shifts and becomes genuinely scary as new types of undead emerge while also reducing your visibility by a lot. The game feels especially scary early on when you don't have many character upgrades and it's difficult to run away from these threats at night, making night-time missions extremely dangerous.
- The gameplay is probably the main focus of the game, with fast and smooth parkour animations, alongside extremely gory combat featuring decapitations and the desmembering of enemies depending on your chosen weapon types.

Cons:
- The story isn't very good in my opinion, being both short and quite predictable.
- Gameplay becomes a bit repetitive if you end up deciding to constantly use a special tool given to you later in the game, that considerably speeds up parkour and in some cases even gets rid of threats completely by making you move way too fast.
- Weapons durability can be annoying as each weapon can only be repaired a set ammount of times, and refurbishing them is an annoying process as it requires doing specific escort missions.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience performance issues including frame rate drops, freezing, and lag spikes in dense areas.

citations.review_text:
this is one of my all time favorite games ever in the history of ever.
PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE FIX THE FRAME PROBLEM!!!
for the first 50 hours or so, the DL was running smoothly, until my ♥♥♥♥ randomly started slowing down and even freezin at times and the frame rate drops down into less than 5 FPS. literally making the game unplayable.
i would easily have like 500 hours DL if i could play the damn game.

Dying Light with it's following dlc "The Following" (which I honestly liked a lot better than base game itself, where they even introduced a drivable/modifyable buggy) seems to really hold the title of the "ultimate zombie game" out there.

The few minor cons would be:
- Huge lag spikes in certain town-ish spots with lots of meaty zombies
- Terrain issues where, when u grapple something, you can sorta feel like it goes out of immersion due to impossible grabs and throws
- A lot of times, at least for me (if it weren't for my veteran friends assists), you could easily get lost on where to go or what to do, because objectives sometimes are faulty and not always intuitive

If I give base game a solid 8/10, then "The Following" dlc easily tops it off with better rating, where as of now, I give that - 9.5/10.

Co-op was definitely super fun to experience in this game however, and I hope other game studios follow it's similar premise/formula (perhaps even with slight tweaks of their own) to make more titles just like this one.

One of the most boring games I have played.  Just endless pick up stuff, make stuff, it breaks, make more stuff.  The magic people problem is the laziest.  You kill zombies, they respawn behind you almost immediately, so unrealistic.  Combat is awful.  UI is clunky.  Just really disappointed.  Heard good things but this isn't.

Update - just got to Old Town and, wow, the crappiness is just everywhere.  Constantly dying through no fault of your own, horrible parkour, stupid exploding enemies where there's no way you're getting away, how did this nightmare ever get good reviews?  The weapons system is terrible.  The controls and UI continue to frustrate.  This is so bad.  I don't get it.  I was making do with the original town (Slums) and was approaching maybe changing my review to Positive.  But, Old Town is so badly configured, structured, and the parkour/heights so badly programmed, the constant dying from falling just turns the experience into a "Get me back to the Slums as fast as possible".

Wow, just tried to play the quest Searchlights.  That's all I needed to give this a double thumbs down.  What a sadistic quest that's only purpose is to create the emotion anger.   The developer is obviously a sadist that never left the 90's.  I refuse to participate.
